## Correctness/deployment handoff: existing ACK-keyed rows

Removing ACK from the kind set can decrease the computed latest-own sequence for an existing stored stretch. The claim replaces a row only when the incoming sequence is greater (`crates/store/src/stalls.rs:35-40`), while reuse/telling requires exact equality (`crates/daemon/src/modal_stall.rs:117-154`). The sweep does not clear the mismatched row.

For a hypothetical legacy row: own event seq 100 at minute 0, ACK seq 110 at minute 2, then an old-daemon stall claim at minute 22 with PA notification still owed. After upgrade, latest own is 100. Replacement rejects the lower value and retries/new-recipient tells are skipped until a retained own event exceeds 110. Exact-sequence attempt/close guards also cannot update that obsolete stretch; the standing view only checks for newer own events (`crates/store/src/stalls.rs:112-116,147-148,190-194`).

This is a source-confirmed transition defect, not evidence of affected production rows or a new unauthorized injection primitive. Reconcile ACK-keyed persisted rows while preserving stale-round concurrency protection. It does not refute the reported F108 initial-miss timeline, where no stall row had yet been claimed.
